issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE 'python:3.12' is duplicated across Python, a TS constant, and a TS fallback literal.
issues.detail: The default lives in backend/kale/pipeline.py, is redeclared in CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and is hardcoded again as the catch-branch fallback in Commands.ts getDefaultBaseImage. The RPC was supposed to single-source this value; instead the next bump will silently leave stale copies. Trust the RPC and keep at most one clearly-marked emergency fallback.

issues.description: _set_base_image silently changes the pod-introspection-failure fallback from '' (delegate to KFP) to a pinned 'python:3.12'.
issues.detail: Previously an empty string deferred image selection to KFP's own default; the patch now hardcodes python:3.12 on every failing-pod path. This is a real runtime behavior change, not a UI cosmetic, and the commit message advertises only display work. Split the semantic change out and document the new contract for base_image.

issues.description: Replacing the inline base-image Input with a 5%-wide 'IMAGE' button that opens a modal regresses both visibility and editability.
issues.detail: The user could previously read and edit the current base image directly in the panel; now they must open a dialog (and only after naming the step) to see or change it. The 5% width inside an unspecified flex container is fragile, and the change is a UX regression dressed as a feature. Preserve inline visibility/editing for the common case or justify the contract change.

issues.description: InlineMetadata.createBaseImageText now always renders, breaking the prior empty-string contract and re-implementing the precedence chain inline.
issues.detail:
The function used to return '' when no baseImage was set; it now unconditionally renders a

element and reproduces the baseImage / pipelineBaseImage / defaultBaseImage precedence chain that also exists in the Jinja template and dialog placeholder. Non-step cells may now display meaningless base-image text, and the resolution logic should live in a single resolveBaseImage helper with a stated contract.

issues.description: get_default_base_image is an RPC round-trip for a compile-time constant, with a function-local import hiding the module dependency.
issues.detail: The handler imports DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE inside the function body and returns a literal already known at build time, while the client also hardcodes the same value as a fallback. Either bundle the constant at build time or rely on the RPC alone, and move the import to module scope to make the dependency on kale.pipeline honest.

issues.description: DefaultState.defaultBaseImage = '' overloads three states into one string field.
issues.detail: Empty string now means not-yet-loaded, while non-empty can mean either the loaded default or some other value, forcing children into truthy-fallback chains like defaultBaseImage || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE. A discriminated union or nullable type would make the loading invariant explicit instead of smuggling control flow through a sentinel value.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR was sold as a display feature but ships a real runtime behavior change and several structural problems. The two P0s are unanimous: the python:3.12 default is now duplicated across Python, a TS constant, and a TS fallback (defeating the purpose of the new RPC), and _set_base_image silently swaps an empty-string KFP-delegation fallback for a pinned image. The UI also regresses by hiding the current base image behind a modal-opening 5%-wide IMAGE button, and InlineMetadata loses its empty-string contract while re-implementing the precedence chain inline. Recommended action: split into separate patches for the semantic pipeline change, the single-sourced constant, and the UI, and reconsider the button-plus-modal versus the prior inline Input.
